role.altitude: From producing and delivering courses to owning Noordhaven's competence record (who is certified for what, on which site, until when) and the AI Act Article 4 measures file for 1,200 staff, and designing the pipelines that produce, check and assign training.
reach: HR Administrator: certificate expiry tracking and Studytube enrolment admin for forklift, VCA and food safety
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: the training part of the Power BI HR dashboard (completion, certification on first shift, link to 90-day retention)
Recruiter: preboarding and week-one onboarding content for new hires and flex workers
HR Business Partner: manager feedback practice and first-line leader development material
Staffing agency coordination: induction packs and certificate checks for flex workers before their first shift
Compliance: keeping the Article 4 AI literacy measures record for the company
role.ceiling_note: About a third of the role's hours can go (content drafting, material review, admin, evaluation reporting). The rest stays human: practical safety training on the warehouse floor, external certification (VCA, forklift), needs analysis with site managers, works council consent on training policy and monitoring-capable tools, and the trust of shift leads and drivers. Anything that evaluates workers with learning data becomes high-risk under the AI Act from 2 December 2027, which caps autonomy there.
skills_to_grow: Writing and testing prompts and review checklists for Studytube AI Authoring and Copilot
Learning measurement: baselines, six-week and six-month measures agreed with managers, Power BI on the AFAS extract
Simple workflow automation (Power Automate, Studytube and AFAS exports) for expiry-driven enrolment
EU AI Act (Art. 4, 5, 50, Annex III) and WOR article 27 in practice, including drafting works council requests
Content quality review: reading level (B1 Dutch), multilingual versions, safety sign-off routing
Coaching people to use AI to learn rather than delegate
role.ambitious_version: Every shift worker, including flex workers from the three agencies, is certified and briefed in their own language before their first shift, every office worker has a disclosed AI-suggested learning path their manager agrees, and L&D reports quarterly on certified-on-first-shift, week-one onboarding and 90-day retention instead of courses completed, with the Article 4 record kept current for all 1,200 staff.

tasks.short: Run classroom and toolbox sessions, role plays, videos and exercises for warehouse, transport and office staff.

today.trigger: Scheduled training session, new-hire intake or a site manager's request
steps: Pick format and exercises for the group and site
Build or reuse slides, videos and role-play cases
Deliver the session in Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo or on Teams
Run discussion and exercises, answer questions
Record attendance in Studytube
drudgery: Writing fresh role-play cases and quiz questions each time
Re-cutting the same deck for different sites and shifts
Typing up attendance after the session
today.time_sinks: Preparing varied exercises and adapting material for groups with mixed Dutch levels and shift times.

lenses.faster: Copilot drafts role-play cases, discussion prompts and quizzes from the course outline in minutes, so preparation shrinks; delivery time stays the same.
lenses.autonomous: Attendance and quiz results flow from Teams forms into Studytube without retyping.
lenses.ambitious: Every first-line leader gets a practice partner for difficult conversations (absence talks, safety feedback) between sessions, disclosed as AI.
lenses.joy: Less time writing cases, more time in the room coaching people and watching them get it.
lenses.options: Five versions of a role play at different difficulty levels or for different sites, the trainer picks on the day.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs a library of practice scenarios and checks they work, instead of rewriting them for each session.
reach: HR Business Partner: manager feedback practice

tasks.human_edge: Reading the room, building trust with shift workers and drivers, and doing practical safety training on the floor.
tasks.pattern_why: Delivery is done with people; AI helps prepare and gives learners a practice partner, but the trainer leads and practical safety training stays human.

in_practice.trigger: Session scheduled in Studytube or Outlook
steps: Copilot drafts exercises, cases and quiz from the course outline
Trainer edits and picks formats
Trainer delivers; optional AI practice bot for follow-up, labelled as AI
Attendance and quiz results synced to Studytube
in_practice.human_gate: Trainer approves all session material; safety content signed by the site safety lead.
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube session record and SharePoint course folder

evidence.claim: An agent drafting manager feedback against the SBI rubric raised 'Good' write-ups by 16 points for users against 7 for non-users.
An AI assistant raised novice support agents' productivity by 34%.
evidence.source: Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond, NBER w31161 [S3]

evidence.claim: An AI tutor must disclose it is AI; inferring learners' emotions in the workplace is banned.

risks: Learners who let AI do the exercise learn less (17% lower mastery in one trial)
Any webcam or voice emotion analysis in a practice tool is prohibited
Generic AI cases that do not fit Noordhaven's sites lose credibility with shift staff
research_questions: Does a disclosed AI practice partner raise first-line leaders' feedback quality, measured against a baseline before launch?
How much prep time per session do trainers actually save over eight weeks?
Will the works council see the practice tool as monitoring-capable under WOR 27(1)(l)?

tasks.short: Write and update manuals, handouts, e-learnings and visuals for courses in Studytube and on SharePoint.

today.trigger: New process, policy or CAO change, new course request or a material that is out of date
steps: Collect source material from managers, SOPs and SharePoint policies
Write the outline and text
Make handouts, slides and visuals
Build the e-learning and questions in Studytube
Get review from the subject expert and publish
drudgery: Turning dense SOPs into plain language
Writing quiz questions
Making translated versions for flex workers
Keeping versions in step after a policy change
today.time_sinks: First drafts and rework after expert review; translations for non-Dutch speakers.

lenses.faster: Studytube AI Authoring drafts outline, script and questions from the uploaded SOP or PPT; the specialist edits instead of writing from blank.
lenses.autonomous: When a SharePoint policy or SOP changes, a flow flags every linked course and drafts the updated sections for review.
lenses.ambitious: Every warehouse SOP gets a short e-learning and one-page handout in Dutch, English, Polish and Romanian for flex workers, kept current.
lenses.joy: No one misses writing the fortieth multiple-choice question; time goes to making examples that fit the floor.
lenses.options: Three formats from one source: e-learning, toolbox talk card and job aid poster.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the source-to-course pipeline and its review checklist rather than each document.
reach: HR Administrator: policy summaries for the intranet

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what matters on the floor, getting the subject expert's real input, and judging whether material is correct and usable.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured source documents become structured course drafts inside a fixed authoring and approval flow.

in_practice.trigger: Course request or change to a linked SOP or policy in SharePoint
steps: Upload source to Studytube AI Authoring
AI drafts outline, text, questions and translations and checks reading level
Specialist edits and adds site examples
Subject expert and, for safety content, the safety lead approve
Publish in Studytube with version note
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves every course; safety lead signs safety content before publication.
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube course version history and a SharePoint change log

evidence.claim: Studytube AI Authoring drafts outlines, scripts and questions from a title or uploaded PDF, PPT or SCORM; authors edit.
MHR's learning team has an agent draft content and check reading level, with a person reviewing.
Faster content is the top expected AI benefit among L&D practitioners.

risks: Wrong safety instructions published if review is skipped
Translations that miss site jargon
Time spent fixing AI output eats the gain (42% of AI time on troubleshooting in one survey)
research_questions: How long does a 20-minute Studytube course take end to end with AI Authoring against the last five built by hand?
Do flex workers score higher on safety quizzes with materials in their own language?
How many review rounds does the safety lead need on AI-drafted content?

tasks.short: Offer refresher and skills courses, including forklift, VCA and food safety renewals, to shift and office staff.

today.trigger: Certificate nearing expiry, manager request, new equipment or a quality incident
steps: Check expiry lists in Studytube and Excel
Match people to shifts and sites from AFAS rosters
Book courses or external examiners
Send invitations and reminders
Chase no-shows and update records
drudgery: Cross-checking expiry dates against rosters by hand
Rebooking after shift changes
Chasing managers and agencies about who attends
today.time_sinks: Matching certificate expiries with shift rosters across three sites and the flex pool.

lenses.faster: Expiry lists, roster matching and bookings run from rules, so the specialist only handles conflicts.
lenses.autonomous: Ninety days before a forklift or VCA certificate lapses, the system enrols the worker in a session that fits their AFAS roster and notifies the shift lead.
lenses.ambitious: No one starts a shift with a lapsed certificate, flex workers included, and office staff get skills offers matched to their role.
lenses.joy: Gone: the expiry spreadsheet and the reminder emails; left: talking with managers about who needs what.
lenses.options: For each lapse, two or three session slots ranked by roster fit and cost.
lenses.altitude: The specialist designs the certification rules and watches the exceptions dashboard.
reach: Staffing agency coordination: certificate checks for flex workers

tasks.human_edge: Deciding which skills programmes the business needs and persuading site managers to release people from shifts.
tasks.pattern_why: Expiry dates, rosters and course slots are structured; the rules can be written down and outputs checked.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly check of Studytube certificate expiry dates against AFAS rosters
steps: Script lists certificates expiring within 90 days
Matches each worker to sessions that fit the roster
Books and sends invitation to worker and shift lead
Flags conflicts and flex workers to the specialist
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist resolves flagged conflicts; external bodies certify VCA and forklift skills.
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube enrolments and a Power BI exceptions report

evidence.claim: Certificate expiry, enrolment and scheduling fit deterministic software at high autonomy using Studytube expiry dates and AFAS rosters.
Microsoft's Learning agent shows skill gaps, pathways and mentors for staff.
VCA and forklift skills are certified by outside bodies; AI only prepares learners.

risks: Stale roster data books people on the wrong shift
Agency flex workers missing from AFAS fall through
Works council consent needed if the tool can monitor individuals (WOR 27(1)(l))
research_questions: How many shifts last year started with a lapsed certificate, by site?
Can Studytube and AFAS exports be joined reliably on employee number, including flex workers?
What share of bookings would still need manual rescheduling?

tasks.short: Track attendance, evaluations and results of training and report whether programmes work.

today.trigger: End of a course, quarterly HR report or a manager question
steps: Export completions and evaluation forms from Studytube
Clean data in Excel
Read open comments and summarise
Build the report or Power BI page
Discuss results with managers
drudgery: Copying exports into Excel
Reading hundreds of open comments
Rebuilding the same charts each quarter
today.time_sinks: Cleaning exports and summarising comments; there is rarely a baseline to compare against.

lenses.faster: Power BI refreshes from Studytube and AFAS nightly and an LLM clusters open comments into themes in minutes.
lenses.autonomous: Six weeks and six months after a programme, agreed measures are pulled and a summary goes to the manager.
lenses.ambitious: Measure what matters for the North Star: certified on first shift, week-one onboarding, 90-day retention, per programme.
lenses.joy: No more comment spreadsheets; time goes to deciding what to change.
lenses.options: Comment themes cut by site, shift or language group to compare explanations.
lenses.altitude: The specialist sets baselines and measures with managers and owns the evaluation design, not the reports.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: training dashboards

tasks.human_edge: Agreeing with managers what success means before launch and judging cause and effect.
tasks.pattern_why: Numbers are deterministic in Power BI; the LLM turns free-text comments into themes inside that flow, at group level only.

in_practice.trigger: Course end, plus six-week and six-month timers per programme
steps: Nightly refresh of Studytube and AFAS data into Power BI
LLM clusters comments into themes with example quotes, anonymised
Specialist reviews and writes the conclusion
Report shared with the manager and HR team
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist reviews themes before sharing; results stay at group level and never feed appraisals.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI HR dashboard and SharePoint evaluation folder

evidence.claim: MHR agrees measures with the manager first, collects at six weeks and six months, and uses AI to cluster comments as support, not for decisions.
Workday advises setting baselines before launch.
From 2 December 2027 AI using learning data to evaluate workers is high-risk.

risks: Sliding into individual evaluation triggers high-risk duties and works council consent
Small groups make anonymised comments identifiable (AVG/GDPR)
Clustering hides minority but important safety remarks
research_questions: Which three programmes have a usable baseline today?
Does the works council accept comment clustering at group level under WOR 27(1)(k)?
Do LLM themes match a human coder's on a sample of 200 comments?

tasks.short: Design and plan onboarding and training programmes for new hires, shift staff and managers.

today.trigger: Annual training plan, new site process, hiring wave or high early turnover
steps: Talk with site managers and HR Business Partners about needs
Draft programme structure and timing
Align with shift patterns, CAO rules and budget
Plan trainers, rooms and Studytube modules
Get approval and launch
drudgery: Building planning grids around shifts
Rewriting programme documents for each audience
today.time_sinks: Meetings to collect needs and the planning puzzle around shifts and peak season.

lenses.faster: Copilot summarises needs interviews and drafts programme options and planning grids from shift data.
lenses.autonomous: A new hire in AFAS triggers the week-one onboarding path and invitations automatically.
lenses.ambitious: A week-one onboarding that every new hire and flex worker completes, measured against 90-day retention by site.
lenses.joy: Less planning grid work, more time with managers on what new people really struggle with.
lenses.options: Three programme designs (classroom heavy, blended, on-the-job buddy) with cost and shift impact side by side.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns onboarding as a system with measures, not a series of events.
reach: HR Business Partner: leader development design

tasks.human_edge: Understanding the business need, negotiating with site managers and deciding the programme; HR decides executive development.
tasks.pattern_why: Design judgement stays with the specialist; AI speeds research, drafts and options.

in_practice.trigger: Training plan cycle or a request from a site manager or HRBP
steps: Copilot summarises interview notes and exit data
Drafts two or three programme options with schedule
Specialist chooses and adjusts with managers
Approved programme set up in Studytube
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist and HR Director approve programme design; training policy changes go to the works council (WOR 27(1)(f)).
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint training plan and Studytube programme setup

evidence.claim: Microsoft's Learning agent proposes pathways while HR still guides role moves and leadership development.
Most L&D teams use AI for content; core design work holds steady.

risks: Generic programme designs that ignore shift realities
Works council not consulted on training policy changes, risking nullity
Learning paths for office staff must be disclosed as AI suggestions
research_questions: What share of new hires complete onboarding in week one today, by site?
Is there a link between week-one onboarding completion and 90-day retention in the AFAS data?
How many hours per programme go into needs meetings versus drafting?

tasks.short: Compare classroom, e-learning and virtual delivery on effect, cost and travel between sites.

today.trigger: Budget round, new course, or complaints about cost or attendance
steps: Collect costs for trainers, rooms, travel and paid hours
Pull completion and results per format from Studytube
Survey learners and managers
Compare in Excel and write advice
drudgery: Gathering costs from AFAS and agency invoices
Building comparisons by hand
today.time_sinks: Finding cost data, especially paid training hours of flex workers via agency invoices.

lenses.faster: A Power BI cost-per-format model built once from AFAS, Studytube and agency data replaces the yearly Excel exercise.
lenses.autonomous: Cost and result per format refresh each month without anyone collecting data.
lenses.ambitious: Every course has a known cost per certified worker and a delivery choice based on evidence.
lenses.joy: No more invoice hunting; the work is choosing the format.
lenses.options: Scenarios per course: all classroom, blended, all virtual, with cost, travel kilometres and pass rates.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the delivery cost model and its assumptions.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: data model

tasks.human_edge: Weighing what can be learned online against hands-on safety needs and site culture.
tasks.pattern_why: Data collection becomes deterministic; the choice of format is a judgement the specialist makes with AI-built scenarios.

in_practice.trigger: Budget cycle or new course decision
steps: Power BI model pulls cost and results per format
Copilot drafts scenarios and a short advice note
Specialist checks assumptions and decides
Advice shared with HR Director and site managers
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist and HR Director decide the delivery format.
data_needed: Paid training hours incl. flex workers
Completion and pass rates per format

evidence.claim: Cost reports for training fit deterministic software.
No opened source shows a course format change cutting time-to-skill.

risks: Cheap online formats chosen for hands-on skills
Agency invoice data too coarse to split training hours
Pass rates confounded by group differences
research_questions: Can training hours of flex workers be separated in agency invoices?
Do pass rates differ between classroom and e-learning for the same course?
What does a day of cross-site training travel cost today?

tasks.short: Read up on L&D practice, AI in learning, safety rules and Dutch and EU regulation.

steps: Scan newsletters and journals
Read selected articles
Save notes in OneNote or SharePoint
Share relevant items with the team
drudgery: Skimming many newsletters for a few relevant items
Losing track of what was read
today.time_sinks: Filtering volume; checking regulation updates such as the AI Act.

lenses.faster: A weekly digest summarises newsletters and regulation updates with source links; the specialist reads only what matters.
lenses.autonomous: Alerts fire when Studytube, the AI Act guidance or CAO training clauses change.
lenses.ambitious: The team keeps a short, sourced practice file that informs every programme decision.
lenses.joy: Less skimming, more reading the few good pieces in depth.
lenses.options: Summaries of competing views on a question, such as how to build AI literacy.
lenses.altitude: The specialist curates sources and checks the digest instead of hunting.
reach: HR Director: briefings on AI Act duties

tasks.human_edge: Judging what applies to a logistics company with shift workers and turning it into choices.
tasks.pattern_why: Reading and judgement stay with the person; AI filters and summarises.

steps: Collect feeds and newsletters
LLM summarises with links and tags relevance
Specialist reads selected originals
Notes saved to SharePoint practice file
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist checks the original source before acting or sharing.

evidence.claim: Desk workers spend 42% of AI time troubleshooting and 35% say knowledge transfer now runs mainly through AI.
Article 4 AI literacy duty has no set level or certificate; courses selling certificates give a record, not compliance.

risks: Summaries replace reading and understanding
Invented or wrong sources in summaries
Echo chamber from a narrow source list
research_questions: Which sources led to an actual programme change last year?
How often do digest summaries misstate the source on a sample check?

tasks.short: Check outlines, slides and handouts from internal and external trainers before they are used.

today.trigger: Trainer or supplier submits new or updated material
steps: Read the material against learning objectives
Check correctness against SOPs, policies and CAO
Check language level, layout and accessibility
Send feedback and approve
drudgery: Line-by-line checks of language level and format
Cross-checking against current SOPs
today.time_sinks: Careful reading of long decks and back-and-forth with trainers.

lenses.faster: An LLM checks the material against a fixed checklist (objectives covered, B1 language, outdated SOP references, accessibility) and marks issues for the specialist.
lenses.autonomous: Material uploaded to the SharePoint review folder gets an automatic check report before the specialist opens it.
lenses.ambitious: Every external supplier's material is checked on the same standard, including translations.
lenses.joy: The specialist focuses on substance and teaching quality instead of typos and layout.
lenses.options: Suggested rewrites at two language levels for difficult passages.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns and improves the review checklist.

tasks.human_edge: Judging teaching quality and correctness of safety content; giving feedback trainers accept.
tasks.pattern_why: Unstructured material is checked against a written checklist with a structured issue list as output.

in_practice.trigger: Upload to the SharePoint review folder
steps: LLM checks against the checklist and current SOPs
Issue list with suggested fixes produced
Specialist reviews and sends feedback
Safety lead signs off safety content
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves; safety lead signs safety content.

evidence.claim: MHR's agent checks reading level with a person reviewing.
LLMs can check text against a written checklist and flag issues.

risks: Checklist misses errors outside its scope
False confidence in a clean report
Supplier material shared with an AI tool may breach supplier terms
research_questions: What share of issues the specialist found in the last 20 reviews would the checklist catch?
Do supplier contracts allow processing their material with an AI tool?
